keyframe_review.note: 39,924 km2 for 1677-1682 in Cliopatria (a core of 164 cells around Bijapur; the Maratha Empire row begins the same year and takes 136 cells of the 1662 shape, Mysore 215). The pages that speak of these years say: 26 November 1677 Shivaji 'seized most of his possessions on the Mysore plateau' from Venkoji, who held Shahaji's Bijapuri jagir of Bangalore, Kolar, Hoskote and Sira (Shivaji, Shahaji and Ekoji I pages), and Vellore and Gingee 'gave him possession of vast territory in the Mysore plateau and Madras Carnatic, containing 100 forts'; the Adil Shahi page that Shivaji 'undid almost all the southern Bijapuri conquests' and the Marathas had 'de facto control of much of the sultanate's Deccan territory'; the Dharwad page that Dharwad, annexed in 1573, was taken by Aurangzeb in 1685, so the northern Karnataka was still Bijapur's. The correction therefore takes the 1662 shape minus Kolhapur (1675), the whole Karnatak block of 1638-1648 (264 cells, which includes Vellore, Gingee and the Bangalore plateau; /ledger Nov 1677) and the Golconda gains: about 830 cells, roughly 212,000 km2, against Cliopatria's 39,924 km2 (factor 5.3). No page opened lists what Bijapur held in 1677-1686, so the remainder is a minimum correction, not a surveyed map; the reviewer's list (Raichur Doab, Adoni, Bankapur, Dharwar, Belgaum, Gulbarga) is inside it but no page opened names Bankapur, Belgaum or Gulbarga as Bijapuri in these years.

The Krishnadevaraya page gives his death as 17 October 1529 (infobox 'Died: 17 October 1529'), so the recapture falls in 1530, the first year after the death (confidence 2: the page does not print 1530). An earlier note here put the death in 1530; the Krishnadevaraya page says 1529.

region.text: the Raichur Doab with Raichur, Mudgal and Yadgir, the 156 cells that Cliopatria adds to Bijapur in 1521

ledger.note: 1534: Vijayanagara takes the Raichur Doab again. 'Vijayanagara invaded the sultanate and seize the Raichur Doab from the Adil Shahis' in the reign of Mallu Adil Shah (1534-1535).

region.text: about 16 cells added in 1547, mostly the coast between Goa and Karwar

ledger.note: c. 1547: Cliopatria adds about 15 cells of the northern Kanara coast to Bijapur. The Ibrahim Adil Shah I page confirms the movement in his reign (1535-1558) without a year or a place: 'considerable acquisitions were made in the south along the west coast' and 'The farthest point of Bijapur territory now extended south of Goa'. The year 1547 and the cells are Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: the strip of about 11 cells on the Ahmadnagar frontier

ledger.note: c. 1547: about 11 cells at the Solapur-Naldurg edge pass to Ahmadnagar. The Ibrahim Adil Shah I page says that in his reign 'while Bidar was conquered, Solapur and Kalyani were lost to Ahmadnagar' without years (the Adil Shahi page: Burhan Nizam Shah besieged Solapur four times). The 1547 year and the cells are Cliopatria's (confidence 1). Kalyani's loss is not entered (no year); its return is /ledger 1561.

region.text: the strip of about 11 cells on the Ahmadnagar frontier

ledger.note: c. 1552: the Solapur-Naldurg strip returns to Bijapur in Cliopatria's shapes; no page opened dates it.

region.text: Kaliyani (Basavakalyan), 55 km west of Bidar

ledger.note: 1561: Ahmadnagar returns Kaliyani. 'Hussain sued for peace in 1561, submitting to Rama Raya and returning Kaliyani to Ali Adil Shah.' (In 1563 he besieged it again and abandoned the siege.) Cliopatria draws Kaliyani inside Bidar's shape.

region.text: the Raichur Doab with Raichur, Mudgal and Yadgir, the 156 cells that Cliopatria adds to Bijapur in 1521

ledger.note: 1565: the Raichur Doab returns to Bijapur after Talikota. Bijapur defeated Vijayanagara 'in the 1565 Battle of Talikota' and the Raichur Doab 'was returned to Bijapur'; Yadgir and Bagalkote had been negotiated away to Vijayanagara in 1563.

region.text: Adoni and the Carnatic lands of the 1572 shape (366 cells)

ledger.note: 1575: Ali Adil Shah I completes the conquest of the Carnatic. He 'annexed more land from Vijayanagara in a campaign which lasted until 1575', conquering 'Adoni and much of the Carnatic'; 'By 1576, land gained under Ali I had doubled the sultanate's holdings.' Cliopatria dates the shape to 1572.

region.text: the island fortress of Janjira on the Konkan coast

ledger.note: 1618: Bijapur loses Janjira. 'In 1618, the sultan lost the fortress of Janjira to the independent Habshi state of western India.'

region.text: the whole of Bidar around the old Bahmani capital

ledger.note: 1619: Bijapur annexes Bidar. 'In 1619, he [Amir Barid III] was defeated by the Bijapur sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II. Bidar was annexed to Bijapur sultanate.' The Adil Shahi page: 'The following year, Bijapur conquered the neighbouring Bidar Sultanate.'

region.text: the sultanate as it stood in 1636 (the shape of 1619-1639); later gains and losses follow the keyframes

ledger.note: 1636: Bijapur accepts Mughal suzerainty. 'In 1636, Bijapur signed a treaty agreeing to pay tribute to the Mughal emperor' and acknowledge Mughal authority; 'the recent Mughal conquest of Ahmednagar was partitioned between the two states' (the share is not described). The Mohammed Adil Shah of Bijapur page calls it a 'peace treaty of 1636, after the extinction of Ahmednagar' that 'sealed the expansion of Bijapur in the north', and says Shah Jahan recognised his sovereignty and gave him the title of Shah in 1648. No page opened dates a renunciation; the relation is closed at the outbreak of the 1685 war (vassal_end of April 1685). The mughal-empire dossier (sa-05) should carry the mirror vassal_start.

region.text: Bangalore and the Kolar, Hoskote, Doddaballapura and Sira areas of Shahaji's jagir

ledger.note: December 1638: Bijapur takes Bangalore. 'In December 1638, the Bijapur forces seized Bangalore, which was given as a jagir to Shahaji' after 'Bijapur's invasion of Kempe Gowda III's territories'; Shahaji was also given charge of the Kolar, Hoskote, Doddaballapura and Sira areas. The defender is the page's: the Kempe Gowda I page calls the Yelahanka chiefs 'a separate Vijayanagara feudal vassal', so the Aravidu remnant was their overlord. In 1648 Shahaji surrendered the Bangalore fort after his arrest and a letter of 26 May 1658 returned 'his former jagir of Bangalore' (Shahaji page). The region is the researcher's reading of the areas named (an 80 km circle round Bengaluru and a 40 km circle at Sira). Cliopatria shows these lands only from 1653.

region.text: Vellore and the forts round it

ledger.note: 1641: Bijapur's army takes Vellore. 'The Bijapur army captured several other forts, including Vellore, during this campaign', introduced as 'in 1641' (the page does not date Vellore itself). The Abdullah Qutb Shah page says Mir Jumla, as Golconda's wazir, 'helped capture Vellore in 1646'; the pages disagree on the year and on who took it. The Shahaji page is followed.

region.text: the Gingee fort and its country

ledger.note: 1648: Gingee falls to Bijapur. 'In 1648, Gingee fell to the Adil Shahis' (Mir Jumla II page); the Shahaji page: 'In 1648, during a Bijapur campaign to support the rebellion of the Nayakas against the Vijayanagara king... the forces of Bijapur and Golconda laid siege to the Jinjee fort'.

region.text: the valley of Javali

ledger.note: 1656: Shivaji takes the Javali valley. He 'seized the valley of Javali', after killing Chandrarao More. Shivaji's polity has no Cliopatria row before the Maratha Empire's 1677 (his coronation: 6 June 1674).

region.text: Bidar, Kalyani and the north-eastern lands (112 cells) that Cliopatria moves to the Mughal shape

ledger.note: 1657: the Mughals take Bidar. Bijapur was 'invaded by Mughal forces in 1657 under viceroy Aurangzeb, who captured Bidar and other forts'. Cliopatria removes the 112 cells in 1659.

region.text: Thanjavur and the cities taken from the Nayakas

ledger.note: 1659: Ali Adil Shah II's campaign against Thanjavur begins. He 'captured Thanjavur and other cities from the Nayakas from 1659 to 1663'; Cliopatria keeps the Nayaks of Thanjavur as an independent state to 1676.

region.text: the Pune-Satara-Konkan lands (124 cells) lost to Shivaji

ledger.note: 10 November 1659: Shivaji destroys Afzal Khan's army and takes Pratapgad's country and Panhala. Afzal Khan was sent 'in 1659, but he was murdered'; the two met on 10 November 1659 and 'Shivaji's forces decisively defeated the Bijapur Sultanate's forces' at Pratapgad, 'seizing Panhala fort' the same year. Cliopatria removes 124 cells in 1662 and gives them to the Mughals; the holder was Shivaji.

region.text: Panhala fort

ledger.note: 22 September 1660: Shivaji hands Panhala back. He 'handed over the fort on 22 September 1660' (and retook it in 1673).

region.text: Thanjavur and the cities taken from the Nayakas

ledger.note: 1663: the Thanjavur campaign ends ('captured Thanjavur and other cities from the Nayakas from 1659 to 1663').

region.text: Panhala fort

ledger.note: 1673: Shivaji retakes Panhala. 'He retook Panhala in 1673.'

region.text: the Bijapuri fort of Ponda

ledger.note: April 1675: Shivaji takes Ponda. The page lists 'the Bijapuri forts of Ponda (April 1675)'.

ledger.note: July 1675: Shivaji takes Kolhapur and Karwar. The same campaign: Karwar 'mid-year' and Kolhapur 'July'. Karwar lies outside Cliopatria's 1662 shape.

region.text: Vellore and Gingee

ledger.note: 1677: Shivaji invades Karnataka and seizes Vellore and Gingee. 'In 1677, Shivaji invaded Karnataka'... 'Proceeding south, Shivaji seized the forts of Vellore and Gingee.' The page does not say whose they were; Bijapur had taken both in 1641 and 1648.

the Karnatak conquests of 1638-1648 that Cliopatria adds to Bijapur in 1653 (264 cells: Bangalore, Kolar, Vellore, the Gingee country and the plateau between)

region.text: the Mysore plateau: Bangalore, Kolar, Hoskote, Sira and the rest of the Karnatak conquests of 1638-1648

ledger.note: November 1677: Shivaji takes the Mysore plateau. He 'defeated his half-brother's army on 26 November 1677 and seized most of his possessions on the Mysore plateau' (Shivaji page; the Ekoji I page puts the battle at Valikandapuram on 16 November 1677 and says territories round Bangalore were returned to Dipa Bai in the later treaty); the conquest of Gingee and Vellore 'gave him possession of vast territory in the Mysore plateau and Madras Carnatic, containing 100 forts'. The half-brother Venkoji held Shahaji's Bangalore-Kolar-Hoskote-Sira jagir (Shahaji page; Ekoji I page: 'He succeeded to the Karnataka portion of Shahaji's jagir, that is Bengaluru and Thanjavur') and had taken Thanjavur in January 1676. No page says Bijapur gave up the jagir in 1676, so the loss is entered at Shivaji's conquest; the Adil Shahi page says Shivaji 'undid almost all the southern Bijapuri conquests'. The region is the 1638-1648 Karnatak block (264 cells of Cliopatria's 1653 shape) with the jagir circles, the researcher's reading of 'the Mysore plateau and Madras Carnatic'.

region.text: the same land as the 1636 vassal_start

ledger.note: April 1685: the 1636 tribute relation is over when Aurangzeb declares war. The Siege of Bijapur page says Sikandar Adil Shah 'had refused to be a vassal of the Mughal Empire' and that Aurangzeb responded by declaring war; the refusal is undated, so the end is entered at the siege's start (15 April 1685, confidence 2). The Mughal invasion of 1657 (Adil Shahi page) and the Maratha alliance had already strained it; no page opened gives a renunciation or a resumption between. The mughal-empire dossier (sa-05) should carry the mirror vassal_end.

region.text: Bijapur fort and the country round it

ledger.note: 12 September 1686: Bijapur surrenders; 'The siege of Bijapur began in April 1685 and ended in September 1686 with a Mughal victory.'

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa (1510)
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory: Goa taken in 1510, retaken by Yusuf Adil Shah two months later and conquered again in November 1510.

wars.name: Battle of Raichur
wars.outcome: Decisive Vijayanagara victory on 19 May 1520; Krishnadevaraya occupies Bijapur for a time.
wars.note: The Adil Shahi page: Krishnadevaraya 'occupied Bijapur for an extended period'.

zones.text: the Raichur Doab with Raichur, Mudgal and Yadgir, the 156 cells that Cliopatria adds to Bijapur in 1521

wars.outcome: Ismail Adil Shah recaptures Raichur and Mudgal in 1530; Vijayanagara seizes the Raichur Doab in 1534.

wars.name: Ahmadnagar-Bijapur wars over Solapur and Kaliyani
wars.outcome: Burhan Nizam Shah I's fourth invasion of 1553 reached nearly to Bijapur; Kaliyani returned to Bijapur in 1561; Hussain's 1563 siege of Kaliyani abandoned; 'Another conflict between Ahmednagar and Bijapur arose in 1567', a stalemate. Solapur stays with Ahmadnagar.

wars.name: Bijapur-Portuguese war of 1570-71
wars.outcome: Ali Adil Shah I's conflict with the Portuguese, which he lost; no territory changed hands.

wars.outcome: Shah Jahan besieges Bijapur in 1631 (first Mughal invasion); in 1636 Bijapur signs a treaty to pay tribute; Aurangzeb captures Bidar and other forts in 1657.
wars.note: Aurangzeb's unsuccessful 1637 siege is on the Siege of Bijapur page. The 1636 partition of the Ahmadnagar remnant is on the Adil Shahi page.

wars.outcome: Bijapur takes Bangalore (December 1638), Vellore (1641) and Gingee (1648, with Golconda's help).

notes: Bijapur (14 Cliopatria shapes, 1492-1686; 9-page budget, ten pages opened). No page gives an area: the Adil Shahi page has none and the Siege of Bijapur page lists no holdings, so the infobox comparison could not be made. Cliopatria's shapes disagree with the pages in these places: (1) Gulbarga is inside the 1492 shape but was annexed in 1504; (2) the Raichur Doab is Bijapur's in 1521-1546 in Cliopatria, but Vijayanagara won Raichur in 1520, Bijapur recovered it in 1530, lost it in 1534 and regained it after Talikota (1565); the pre-1520 Bijapuri status of Raichur is not shown by Cliopatria; (3) the Carnatic gain of 1572 is dated by the page to a campaign ending in 1575; (4) Bijapur's Karnataka conquests (Bangalore December 1638, Vellore 1641, Gingee 1648) appear in Cliopatria only in 1653; (5) the 1670 shape (39,645 km2) drops everything south of the Krishna and Kolhapur and Ponda, which the Shivaji page shows Bijapur holding until 1675, and Vellore and Gingee until 1677: the 1670, 1677 and 1683 shapes are corrected to the 1662 shape minus the places the pages show lost, but that is a minimum correction, not a map of Bijapur's real holdings 1677-1686, which no page opened describes; (6) the 1662 loss of the Pune-Satara-Konkan lands is given to the Mughals by Cliopatria; the Shivaji page shows Shivaji took them (1656-1659); Shivaji's polity has no Cliopatria row before the Maratha Empire's 1677 (coronation 6 June 1674), so sa-05 should cover 1656-1676 or the Maratha dossier should start earlier. Overlaps: the 1640 Nellore cells overlap Golconda's Mir Jumla conquests (April 1642); Kaliyani is inside Bidar's shape in 1561; the 1561 return of Kaliyani and the 1563 cession of Yadgir and Bagalkote to Vijayanagara are not drawn (Yadgir is inside the Doab region subtracted 1534-1564). Mughal tributary status: Bijapur agreed in 1636 to pay tribute; the mughal-empire dossier (sa-05) should carry vassal_start 1636 and an end in 1657 or 1686; Bijapur's share of the 1636 partition of the Ahmadnagar remnant is undefined on every page and is not entered. Aravidu Vijayanagara is the counterpart for Bijapur's gains of 1638-1648 although Cliopatria's Vijayanagara ends in 1571; the Talikota page says the Aravidu state disintegrated in the late 1640s. Not opened: Portuguese Goa, Janjira, Basavakalyan, Adoni, Yadgir, Mustafa Khan, Ali Adil Shah I and Ibrahim II articles. The Janjira (Habshi) state has no dossier. Gazetteer names needed: Janjira, Karwar. || FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review): (1) vassal_start 1636 and vassal_end April 1685 added for mughal-empire (the 1685 end from the Siege of Bijapur page: Sikandar 'had refused to be a vassal'; not the 1657 or 1665-66 wars, which no page ties to the tribute). (2) The 1677-1686 shapes no longer keep the Mysore plateau: the new Nov 1677 loss to maratha-empire (Shivaji, Shahaji, Ekoji I pages) subtracts the 264-cell Karnatak block of 1638-1648 and the Bangalore jagir; the 1686 loss and dissolve use that corrected 1683 shape (about 830 cells, roughly 212,000 km2, factor 5.3 over Cliopatria's 39,924 km2). No page opened lists Bijapur's holdings in 1677-1686: the remainder is a minimum correction. (3) Keyframes 1512 (Raichur and Mudgal held to 1520), 1572/_1575 (the 1552 shape for 1572-1574), 1619/_1638 (Bangalore), 1640/_1641/_1642/_1646/_1648/_1650 (Vellore, Gingee, and Golconda's Nellore, Udayagiri and Gandikota gains subtracted so the two dossiers do not overlap) and _1530 added or adjusted. (4) Bangalore's counterpart is the page's 'Kempe Gowda III (Yelahanka Nayakas)'. (5) Not entered: Bijapur's share of the 1636 partition of Ahmadnagar (no page gives it); the 1563 cession of Yadgir and Bagalkote (the Adil Shahi page gives no year, the Ali Adil Shah I page does not mention it); Dharwad's loss to Aurangzeb in 1685 (Dharwad page; inside the 1686 loss). Vellore is 1641 on the Shahaji page and 1646 on the Abdullah Qutb Shah page.
